paragraphs: The paper proposes a model of how the hippocampal formation could learn to interpret sensory experiences and predict what comes next. It connects generative modeling with the hippocampus’s proposed role in spatial and non-spatial memory, using a biologically plausible network that processes a stream of inputs over time.

The central mechanism is rhythmic control of information flow. Theta-band oscillations, operating at 5–10 Hz, switch the direction in which information travels through the network. This supports learning similar to a rapidly alternating wake-sleep procedure in a Helmholtz machine. The same local learning rule supports both inferring hidden states from sensory information and generating sensory predictions.

The model accurately infers latent environmental states and produces realistic sensory predictions in the reported demonstrations. It also learns path integration by developing a ring-shaped connectivity structure consistent with earlier theoretical proposals, and can transfer that structure between environments. These results show how several hippocampal functions can coexist within one biologically plausible computational model.
neurips-2023-a-generative-model-of-the-h.tldr: A hippocampal model uses theta-controlled information flow and local learning to infer hidden states, predict sensory inputs, and learn path integration.

paragraphs: BayesDAG addresses causal discovery while keeping track of uncertainty about which causal explanation is correct. Rather than returning only one graph, Bayesian causal discovery seeks a posterior distribution over possible graphs and their associated functions. This is computationally difficult because graph structures are discrete, must have no directed cycles, and may involve nonlinear relationships.

The framework combines stochastic gradient Markov chain Monte Carlo with variational inference. It samples directed acyclic graphs directly, alongside parameters for the functions connecting variables, without needing a regularizer to encourage acyclicity. A new equivalence with permutation-based graph learning makes it possible to use relaxed gradient estimators over permutations.

This construction supports both linear and nonlinear causal models while addressing restrictions of earlier approaches described in the abstract. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate effectiveness against leading baselines. The contribution is a way to make joint uncertainty over causal structure and functional relationships more computationally accessible while ensuring that sampled graphs are acyclic.
neurips-2023-bayesdag-gradient-based-pos.tldr: BayesDAG combines gradient-based sampling and variational inference to infer uncertainty over valid causal graphs and their linear or nonlinear relationships.

paragraphs: Bounce tackles optimization problems with many input variables, including combinations of discrete choices and other variable types. Such problems arise in applications including materials discovery, hardware design, neural architecture search, and portfolio optimization. The objective is treated as a black box, so the optimizer must search without relying on an explicit formula for its behavior.

The paper first identifies a reliability problem in leading Bayesian optimization methods. Their performance can decline substantially when the unknown best solution lacks a particular structure. This means that strong performance on some problems may depend on properties of the optimum that are unavailable to the optimizer beforehand.

Bounce introduces a mapping of different variable types into nested embeddings whose dimensionality increases. This supplies a common search construction for combinatorial and mixed spaces. Across the reported high-dimensional experiments, Bounce consistently reaches, and often exceeds, state-of-the-art performance. The findings support its empirical reliability across varied problems, addressing the structural sensitivity highlighted by the authors’ analysis.
neurips-2023-bounce-reliable-high-dimens.tldr: Bounce uses nested embeddings of increasing dimensionality to make Bayesian optimization more reliable across high-dimensional combinatorial and mixed-variable problems.

paragraphs: Bullying10K is a dataset intended to support recognition of violent incidents while addressing privacy concerns associated with conventional surveillance imagery. It uses Dynamic Vision Sensors, which record changes in pixel brightness instead of capturing static images. This makes the sensor representation central to the paper’s approach to privacy-conscious recognition.

The dataset contains varied actions, complicated movements, and occlusions drawn from real-life scenarios. Its scale is substantial: 10,000 event segments contain 12 billion events and occupy 255 GB. These recordings provide material for developing systems that interpret human activity from event streams.

The authors define three benchmark tasks: recognizing actions, locating actions in time, and estimating human poses. Together, these cover identifying what happens, determining when it happens, and describing body configuration. The contribution is a shared resource for training and evaluating neuromorphic methods across these tasks. Its stated privacy motivation rests on the sensing approach, while the dataset’s variety and complexity create challenges for methods that must recognize activity despite movement and occlusion.
neurips-2023-bullying10k-a-large-scale-n.tldr: Bullying10K provides event-sensor recordings and three benchmarks for developing privacy-conscious systems that recognize violent activity and human movement.

paragraphs: The paper examines how reliably a test set can reveal model performance for small subgroups or changed deployment conditions. A subgroup may contain too few test examples for an accurate estimate, and available examples may not represent the distribution encountered after deployment. Both problems affect assessments of fairness and reliability.

The proposed framework, 3S Testing, uses deep generative modeling to construct synthetic test sets. It generates examples for underrepresented subgroups and simulates plausible distributional shifts. Its purpose is to improve estimates of an existing model’s performance, making synthetic data part of the evaluation process.

In the reported experiments, this approach estimates performance more accurately than traditional baselines, including evaluation using real test data alone. It also supplies intervals around its estimates that cover the true performance more successfully than existing approaches. These findings support considering synthetic test data when real evaluation data are sparse or mismatched. The broader suggestion of moving toward synthetic evaluation remains a question raised by the results.
neurips-2023-can-you-rely-on-your-model-.tldr: 3S Testing generates synthetic evaluation data to improve performance estimates for small subgroups and plausible deployment shifts.

paragraphs: This paper studies collaboration among agents that each want to improve their own model. Each agent has its own training data, but can also benefit from other agents’ expertise. The proposed method exchanges that expertise through predictions on a shared collection of unlabeled auxiliary examples.

The agents collectively assign pseudo-labels to these examples, which then support learning through distillation. A central trust-weighting mechanism adjusts how much each collaborator contributes to the labels until the group reaches a prediction consensus. This gives the method a way to account for differences in collaborator quality while combining their knowledge.

Experiments show substantial improvements in individual models on the target domain represented by the auxiliary data. The authors also prove that the approach can mitigate the harm caused by bad models in the group. Because collaboration operates through predictions, the design accommodates different model architectures. It also substantially lowers communication overhead relative to typical collaborative learning methods, making the exchange of expertise less demanding.
neurips-2023-collaborative-learning-via-.tldr: Agents improve their individual models by learning from shared pseudo-labels formed through adaptively trust-weighted prediction consensus.

paragraphs: The paper compresses data by representing a signal as a neural network that maps coordinates to values. For an image, this means mapping pixel positions to colors. Fitting a compact network to a particular signal allows its weights to serve as the compressed representation, but reducing weight precision can substantially damage reconstruction quality.

The authors instead fit a variational Bayesian neural network and encode an approximate posterior weight sample using relative entropy coding. This changes how the learned representation is compressed. Minimizing the beta-ELBO directly optimizes the balance between storage rate and reconstruction distortion, with beta controlling different trade-offs for the same network architecture.

The method also learns prior weight distributions through an iterative algorithm and progressively refines the variational posterior. These additions significantly improve performance according to the abstract. Image and audio experiments show strong compression results while retaining a simple approach. The central contribution is to connect probabilistic weight representations, coding, and the desired compression-quality trade-off within one optimization strategy.
neurips-2023-compression-with-bayesian-i.tldr: Bayesian neural signal representations and relative entropy coding enable direct optimization of compression rate against reconstruction quality.

paragraphs: The paper asks when observational data can reveal hidden variables and the causal hierarchy connecting them. The setting is challenging because observed measurements arise from causally related latent variables through nonlinear relationships. Some hidden variables may have no directly observed children, so their influence must be understood through the wider hierarchy.

The authors establish identification guarantees under assumptions they describe as mild. Their permitted structures can contain multiple paths between variables, relaxing earlier latent-tree restrictions. The functions can be generally nonlinear, and variables can be multidimensional and continuous, reducing reliance on restrictive parametric descriptions.

The analysis begins with an identification criterion for an elementary latent-variable model and builds an explicit estimation procedure for the hierarchy. The resulting guarantee is asymptotic, and latent variables are identifiable up to invertible transformations. Thus, recovery allows changes of representation that preserve information rather than requiring one unique numerical coordinate system. The contribution establishes conditions under which both hidden structure and hidden variables can be recovered within this broader nonlinear setting.
neurips-2023-identification-of-nonlinear.tldr: The paper establishes conditional, asymptotic identification of nonlinear latent causal hierarchies, recovering hidden variables up to invertible transformations.

paragraphs: M4 addresses the difficulty of judging whether an explanation faithfully reflects a neural network’s prediction. Feature attribution methods identify input features associated with a prediction, but their evaluation is complicated by differences between model types and by the absence of ground-truth explanations. This makes consistent comparison across settings difficult.

The benchmark evaluates attribution methods with a common set of faithfulness metrics across images and text, and across ResNets, MobileNets, and Transformers. It also organizes existing evaluation metrics into three categories according to the ground truth they require. That taxonomy helps distinguish what information different assessments depend on.

The authors implement established and newer attribution methods through InterpretDL and conduct extensive comparisons to create benchmark baselines. These experiments support broader evaluation across methods, metrics, and architectures, and yield observations relevant to attribution design. The abstract does not identify one universally strongest method; the stated contribution is a unified evaluation resource, accompanied by publicly available implementations of explanation methods and metrics.
neurips-2023-mathcal-m-4-a-unified-xai-b.tldr: M4 standardizes faithfulness evaluation of feature attribution methods across image and text inputs, network architectures, and evaluation metrics.

paragraphs: FedSTO addresses federated object detection when labeled data are available only at a central server and all client data are unlabeled. Client distributions also differ from one another and from the server, for example because of weather conditions. This combines the difficulty of learning without local labels with the difficulty of distribution shifts.

The method uses two training stages: selective training followed by full-parameter training with orthogonality enhancement. Selectively refining the detector’s backbone is intended to avoid overfitting. Orthogonality regularization encourages representation divergence, while local exponential-moving-average mechanisms support the assignment of high-quality pseudo-labels to client examples.

Evaluations on BDD100K, Cityscapes, and SODA10M report state-of-the-art results for the proposed approach. With only 20–30% of labels, FedSTO performs nearly as well as fully supervised centralized training in the reported experiments. These results support the feasibility of learning across heterogeneous clients with no local labels, while retaining labeled supervision at the server as a central part of the setup.
neurips-2023-navigating-data-heterogenei.tldr: FedSTO trains federated object detectors with server-only labels and unlabeled heterogeneous clients, approaching centralized supervised performance in reported experiments.

paragraphs: The paper develops a theoretical account of how score-based diffusion models generalize beyond their training samples. These models connect an unknown target distribution, represented by observed data, with a known prior through a stochastic transport process. The analysis follows how the generalization gap changes during training.

The authors derive estimates suggesting an error rate of O(n^(-2/5) + m^(-4/5)), where n is sample size and m is model capacity, when training is stopped early. The stated rate does not depend on data dimension. Early stopping is therefore part of the result’s conditions, and the estimate connects generalization to both data availability and model capacity.

The analysis also considers a sequence of target densities whose modes become increasingly separated. This data-dependent setting explains an adverse effect of shifting modes on generalization. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical estimates presented in the paper. Together, the results connect training duration and target-distribution geometry to generalization, providing a more quantitative basis for understanding diffusion models.
neurips-2023-on-the-generalization-prope.tldr: The paper derives dimension-independent generalization estimates for early-stopped diffusion models and analyzes how increasing separation between target modes harms generalization.

paragraphs: The paper studies mechanism design when agents’ valuations follow an unknown, possibly correlated distribution. A designer has a reference distribution and wants a truthful mechanism that performs well for true distributions nearby in total variation distance. The question is how sensitive incentive and performance properties are to this distributional uncertainty.

Using a duality property of total variation distance, the authors establish strong robustness results for dominant-strategy and Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms with bounded objectives. The bounded-objective condition is part of the stated result. Its significance is breadth: the analysis covers objectives beyond revenue and explicitly accommodates correlations between agents’ valuations.

Applications include approximately revenue-optimal, approximately Bayesian incentive-compatible mechanisms for weak dependence, and correlation-robust mechanisms from noisy marginal information. The framework also preserves prophet-inequality-type guarantees for correlated priors. Further results give a necessary condition for an infinite revenue gap between simple and optimal mechanisms, and a condition under which simple mechanisms approximate optimal revenue for a single agent with a Markov-random-field type distribution.
neurips-2023-on-the-robustness-of-mechan.tldr: Total variation duality yields robustness results for truthful mechanisms with bounded objectives under uncertainty about correlated valuation distributions.

paragraphs: This paper develops mathematical guarantees for how accurately complex-valued neural networks can approximate functions. It addresses a gap between their promising empirical applications and the comparatively limited theory supporting them. The focus is expressive capacity: how approximation error changes as the number of neurons grows.

The results cover activations that are smooth and non-polyharmonic on some nonempty open set, including modReLU and complex cardioid activations. For a target function with smoothness k and complex input dimension n, the main approximation rate scales as m^(-k/(2n)), where m is the number of neurons. Smoother targets improve this rate, while greater input dimension worsens it.

Under a continuity assumption, the authors show that this rate is optimal, and they discuss optimality when that assumption is removed. They also prove that continuous methods for approximating C^k functions inevitably face the curse of dimensionality. The contribution therefore supplies both quantitative approximation guarantees and a principled account of the dimensional difficulty remaining in this setting.
neurips-2023-optimal-approximation-using.tldr: The paper establishes approximation rates for a broad class of complex-valued networks and proves conditional optimality and dimensionality barriers.

paragraphs: PolyDiffuse reconstructs polygonal geometry from visual sensor data by treating reconstruction as conditional generation with a diffusion model. Structured geometry creates a special difficulty: a set of polygons or polylines can be listed in many equivalent orders. Those alternative representations make the denoising process ambiguous.

Reconstruction also needs noise initialization suited to recovering a particular solution from the observations. The proposed Guided Set Diffusion Model learns guidance networks during forward diffusion to control noise injection and keep permutation variants distinct. During reverse diffusion, those networks initialize and guide the reconstruction while conditioning it on sensor data.

The authors evaluate floorplan reconstruction, represented as sets of polygons, and autonomous-driving HD map reconstruction, represented as sets of polylines. Experiments on standard benchmarks report substantial advances over the state of the art. The contribution is a diffusion formulation that directly addresses both set-representation ambiguity and the need for observation-specific reconstruction, enabling the model to produce structured geometry from sensor inputs.
neurips-2023-polydiffuse-polygonal-shape.tldr: PolyDiffuse guides noise injection and denoising to reconstruct polygonal floorplans and maps while resolving ambiguities caused by equivalent set orderings.

paragraphs: The paper examines a failure of behavior cloning in partially observable environments. An agent learns from observation histories because a single observation may not contain enough information to choose an action. This setup assumes that the history sufficiently captures the information needed to imitate an expert.

Problems arise when the history also reveals previously executed actions. A cloned policy can end up copying its own past behavior instead of producing the appropriate expert action. The authors introduce Past Action Leakage Regularization, or PALR, which uses conditional independence to reduce this unwanted dependence on leaked action information.

The paper compares several versions of the framework using different conditional-independence measures and estimators. That comparison favors a particular kernel-based estimator. Extensive benchmark experiments show substantial improvements over earlier related methods. The findings support regularizing how a policy uses observation history in offline imitation learning, where it must learn without interacting with the environment, and specifically when past-action leakage interferes with learning expert behavior.
neurips-2023-regularized-behavior-clonin.tldr: PALR uses conditional-independence regularization to reduce behavior cloning’s tendency to copy past actions leaked through observation histories.

paragraphs: Transfer-based adversarial attacks create examples using a surrogate model and then apply them to other models without accessing those targets. This paper investigates how the surrogate’s backward computation affects that transfer. The authors focus on nonlinear layers that truncate gradients, including ReLU and max-pooling.

They hypothesize that this truncation weakens the relationship between input gradients and the loss, thereby reducing adversarial transferability, and report empirical support for that hypothesis. Their Backward Propagation Attack changes the backward rules: it uses a non-monotonic function in place of the ReLU derivative and temperature-controlled softmax to smooth the max-pooling derivative.

These modifications aim to preserve more information as gradients propagate backward through the surrogate. Experiments on ImageNet show substantially improved transferability, and the method can be used with existing transfer-based attacks. The contribution identifies backward propagation as an important component of transfer performance and supplies a concrete way to alter it, with the effectiveness established empirically in the reported evaluation.
neurips-2023-rethinking-the-backward-pro.tldr: BPA modifies surrogate-model backward rules to reduce gradient information loss and empirically improve adversarial transferability.

paragraphs: The paper studies reinforcement learning when decisions must satisfy safety constraints despite uncertainty about environmental dynamics. It represents that uncertainty with a distribution over transition models. A risk-averse perspective then accounts for unfavorable possibilities within this uncertainty, using coherent distortion risk measures.

The authors prove that their framework is equivalent to a specific class of distributionally robust safe reinforcement learning problems. This equivalence provides robustness guarantees for the formulation. At the same time, it avoids minimax optimization, enabling an efficient model-free implementation that uses standard data collection from a single training environment.

Experiments examine continuous-control tasks with safety constraints and test the learned behavior in perturbed environments. The reported results show robust performance and safety across a range of those deployment conditions. The significance is the combination of a theoretical robustness interpretation with a comparatively accessible training procedure. The guarantees concern the identified problem class, while the deployment findings provide empirical evidence across the tested perturbations.
neurips-2023-risk-averse-model-uncertain.tldr: A risk-averse treatment of uncertain dynamics yields a safe reinforcement learning framework with distributional robustness guarantees and no minimax optimization.

paragraphs: The paper considers systems whose states combine genuinely stochastic components with pseudo-stochastic components. The latter evolve deterministically once the stochastic states or transitions are given. This structure appears in manufacturing, communication, and queueing networks, and provides an opportunity to extract more learning value from observed transitions.

The proposed model-free reinforcement learning method trains on both real samples and augmented samples. Exploiting the mixed-system structure reduces the required data coverage: real observations only need sufficient coverage of the stochastic states. Augmentation addresses gaps in coverage of the pseudo-stochastic part of the system.

For fitted Q iteration, the authors derive an optimality-gap rate of O(1/sqrt(n) + 1/sqrt(m)), with n real samples and m augmented samples per real sample. Without augmentation, the stated insufficient-coverage setting leaves an O(1) gap. Experiments on multiple queueing-network applications show accelerated learning for both deep Q-learning and deep policy-gradient methods. The result connects a specific structural property of the dynamics to improved sample efficiency.
neurips-2023-sample-efficient-reinforcem.tldr: For systems with conditionally deterministic state components, sample augmentation reduces coverage requirements and accelerates reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: This paper studies distributed finite-sum optimization with one master node and n−1 local nodes. Its assumptions include delta-similarity and mu-strong convexity, linking the analysis to similarity among local problems and curvature of the objective. The central performance measure is communication complexity across the distributed system.

The first algorithm, SVRS, combines gradient sliding with variance reduction. Its communication bound is approximately n + sqrt(n) delta/mu, with logarithmic factors suppressed. The accelerated version, AccSVRS, uses the Katyusha X framework and achieves approximately n + n^(3/4) sqrt(delta/mu), again suppressing logarithmic factors.

The authors emphasize that these bounds are smoothness-free and improve on existing results in ill-conditioned cases. They also establish a lower bound that nearly matches AccSVRS, indicating that its communication requirements are close to the theoretical limit in the analyzed setting. The contribution therefore combines new methods with evidence of near-tightness, clarifying how similarity between distributed objectives can reduce the communication needed for optimization.
neurips-2023-stochastic-distributed-opti.tldr: SVRS and AccSVRS improve communication bounds for distributed strongly convex optimization under similarity assumptions, with a nearly matching lower bound for AccSVRS.

paragraphs: The Temporal Graph Benchmark provides datasets and evaluation procedures for learning on networks that change over time. Its large datasets span years and cover social, trade, transaction, and transportation networks. Tasks include predictions about both nodes and edges, with evaluation protocols designed around realistic uses.

The authors benchmark common models across these datasets and find that performance varies sharply between them. For predicting changing node properties, simple methods often outperform existing temporal graph models. These findings make dataset diversity and strong simple comparisons important parts of assessing progress on temporal graph learning.

TGB also supplies an automated pipeline for data loading, experiment setup, and performance evaluation. Public resources include datasets, example code, evaluation configurations, and leaderboards. This infrastructure supports accessible and reproducible comparisons across different temporal settings. The contribution combines a practical research platform with empirical evidence that success depends strongly on the dataset and task, creating opportunities to understand where current temporal graph methods work well and where they struggle.
neurips-2023-temporal-graph-benchmark-fo.tldr: TGB standardizes temporal graph evaluation and finds large performance differences across datasets, with simple methods often winning on dynamic node prediction.

paragraphs: The paper studies how a voting rule can select a socially desirable outcome when it has limited information about voters’ preferences. Distortion measures how well the rule handles that information gap. The authors focus on assessing voting rules through expected performance under a distribution of voter utilities.

This changes the analytical perspective from the worst-case treatment emphasized in prior work. Expected distortion accounts for how utility configurations are distributed, allowing the analysis to characterize performance averaged over that underlying uncertainty. Expected welfare provides a complementary assessment of the social value produced by the selected outcome.

The main contribution is binomial voting, a new rule accompanied by guarantees for both expected distortion and expected welfare. Those guarantees are distribution-independent, so their stated strength does not rely on selecting one particular underlying utility distribution. The result establishes that this voting rule has strong expected-performance properties across distributions. Its theoretical significance lies in bringing both information loss and achieved welfare into a distribution-based evaluation of voting.
neurips-2023-the-distortion-of-binomial-.tldr: Binomial voting offers distribution-independent guarantees for expected distortion and expected welfare when voters’ preferences are only partially known.

paragraphs: The paper develops a shared framework for segmenting three-dimensional medical images when labels are limited and data distributions differ. Expert annotation of whole volumes is time-consuming, motivating the use of unlabeled data. The intended scope includes semi-supervised learning, unsupervised domain adaptation, and semi-supervised domain generalization.

The authors identify two obstacles: weak learning of features that remain useful across distributions, and training dominated by labeled examples. Their Aggregating & Decoupling framework addresses both. A diffusion encoder aggregates information from multiple distributions into a common knowledge set of invariant features. Three decoders separate aspects of labeled and unlabeled training to reduce overfitting to labeled data, particular domains, and classes.

Evaluation covers four benchmark datasets and four settings, including class-imbalanced semi-supervised learning. The reported results improve on state-of-the-art methods across those settings. These findings support the potential for one framework to handle several related segmentation challenges by sharing cross-domain information while giving labeled and unlabeled learning distinct roles in training.
neurips-2023-towards-generic-semi-superv.tldr: An aggregating encoder and decoupled decoders improve volumetric medical segmentation across limited-label, imbalanced, and shifting-domain settings.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning seeks to remove the influence of selected training examples from an already trained neural network. This paper examines three applications: reducing bias, correcting confusion caused by mislabeled data, and protecting user privacy. It argues that these applications require different definitions of successful forgetting and different ways to measure it.

For privacy evaluation, the authors adapt a strong membership-inference attack to the unlearning setting. They also introduce SCRUB, an unlearning algorithm evaluated across the three applications. This application-dependent evaluation connects the meaning of forgetting to the particular reason data must be removed.

In the reported comparisons, SCRUB is the only method consistently among the strongest performers on forgetting quality across all three applications’ metrics. It also consistently performs well on retained-data accuracy and generalization, while being more efficient than previous work. These empirical findings support its usefulness across several unlearning goals. The contribution combines a broadly competitive algorithm with an evaluation perspective that distinguishes the different outcomes users may need from unlearning.
neurips-2023-towards-unbounded-machine-u.tldr: SCRUB achieves consistently strong empirical forgetting and retained utility across bias removal, mislabeled-data correction, and privacy-oriented unlearning.

paragraphs: The paper develops a unified way to analyze the stability of stochastic optimization algorithms. Stability supports generalization analysis by describing sensitivity to training-data changes. Earlier results often required substantially different proof techniques for different losses or algorithms; this work connects learning theory with applied probability through Wasserstein stability.

Applied to stochastic gradient descent, the approach produces bounds that do not grow with the number of training iterations. The authors obtain results for strongly convex losses and for non-convex losses with additive noise, recovering or extending earlier findings through one technique. The framework relies chiefly on constructing Lyapunov functions, suggesting possible extensions to other optimizers.

The analysis highlights ergodicity as important for time-uniform guarantees and explains why added noise can matter for convex or non-convex problems. An extension of the technique also establishes time-uniform results for SGD without extra additive noise in convex and non-convex settings. Together, these results broaden the available stability analysis while organizing several cases around a common probabilistic approach.
neurips-2023-uniform-in-time-wasserstein.tldr: A unified probabilistic technique yields SGD stability bounds that remain bounded across training iterations in several convex, non-convex, and noisy settings.

paragraphs: UP-DP addresses choosing examples for annotation from an unlabeled dataset in a single pass, before downstream tasks are specified. With a limited labeling budget, the selected examples should provide useful coverage of the data. The paper investigates how vision-language representations can improve this pre-selection process.

Earlier approaches used visual features from foundation models while largely overlooking text features. UP-DP freezes BLIP-2’s parameters and learns text prompts without supervision to improve joint visual-text representations. The learning aims to produce a diverse cluster structure that covers the dataset, connecting prompt adaptation to the choice of examples for labeling.

Comparisons across seven benchmark datasets and different settings report performance gains of up to 20%. The learned prompts also generalize across datasets, directly improving BLIP-2 feature extraction on datasets other than the one used to learn them. These findings support unsupervised prompt learning as a way to adapt the representation used for data selection while keeping the underlying vision-language model fixed.
neurips-2023-up-dp-unsupervised-prompt-l.tldr: UP-DP learns unsupervised text prompts for frozen vision-language models to select diverse labeling examples and transfer improved features across datasets.
